name: riders and leapers
description: Two different armies on a 6x6 board, and no king: a side loses the moment any one of its own three kinds of officer is gone. The riders have two rooks, two bishops and two guards, a guard stepping one square in any direction. The leapers have two champions, which jump one or two squares straight or two diagonally, two knights, and two elephants, which jump one or two squares diagonally. Pawns step one square forward, take one square diagonally forward, and on the last rank promote to one of their own side's officers, so a pawn that gets through can bring back a kind that is about to run out. There is no check and no checkmate, and a player with no legal move draws. Every trade is a question of which kind it leaves short: once a side is down to its last piece of a kind, that piece is worth the game to it, and the other side's plan becomes to hunt it. The armies are short in different places: bishops and elephants each keep to one colour, but a bishop is stopped by whatever stands in its way and an elephant jumps; a rook reaches across the board and a champion only two squares; a guard is slow and a knight cannot be blocked.

provenance.source: docs/reference/extinction-any-kind.md, Q936s: the showcase of per_type own (section 5)
provenance.history: The showcase of schema 27's rules.extinction.per_type "own": Los Alamos's 6x6 board and pawns with no king and two different armies of three paired kinds, riders (rook, bishop, guard) against leapers (champion, knight, elephant), each losing when any one of its own kinds is gone. The second of four drafts: the first had a stronger elephant (one or two squares diagonally or two straight) and the leapers won about three games in four at the stronger budgets; the third and fourth (one rook against one champion, three bishops against three knights) leaned to the riders. Pre-registered in docs/reference/extinction-any-kind.md section 5 before its library measurement. Measured first as 30c055a056ec, whose champion and elephant each wrote their two step lengths as one move; split in two for the rules page, the same game move for move. Joined the library from preview by Q936t (2026-10-17): the library's only game in which each side loses when any one of its own kinds of piece is gone (rules.extinction.per_type "own"), Los Alamos's board and pawns with two different armies instead of the same one, where every trade is a question of which kind it leaves short; viable 4-0 at 0.757.
